title: Credit-Based Flow Control
constraints: The receiver has a 4-entry buffer, so the sender starts with **4 credits**. Each word sent consumes one credit, and each `credit_ret` pulse from the receiver returns one.

`in_ready = (credits != 0)` (combinational). On an edge with `in_valid && in_ready`: `tx_valid <= 1`, `tx_data <= in_data`, and a credit is consumed. Otherwise `tx_valid <= 0`. A consume and a return on the same edge cancel out.
Synchronous reset: 4 credits, `tx_valid = 0`. The receiver never returns more credits than were consumed.
hints: Unlike valid/ready, credits let the link be pipelined over many cycles: the sender never has to see the receiver's ready in the same cycle.
PCIe, NoCs and HBM controllers all use credit-based flow control.

examples.title: net zero
examples.input: send and credit_ret on the same edge
